plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack can achieve dual-band spectral separation (high reflectance 300-450 nm, high transmittance 1000-1700 nm) through thickness optimization alone. The design draws on recalled quarter-wave stack principles adapted for dual-band operation, where the high-index/low-index pair creates a stopband that can be positioned via optical thickness tuning. This route uses no retrieved literature; all justification is from model prior knowledge about dielectric mirror design patterns.

routes.title: 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with refined thickness optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating high-index/low-index dielectric stack with individually optimized thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high reflectance in the 300-450 nm band and high transmittance in the 1000-1700 nm band on fused silica substrate at normal incidence.
routes.design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Alternating high-index (HfO2) and low-index (SiO2) layers create constructive interference for reflection at wavelengths where optical thickness equals quarter-wave multiples. By deviating from strict quarter-wave thicknesses and optimizing each layer individually, the stopband can be broadened toward shorter wavelengths while maintaining transmission at longer wavelengths. The 24-layer count provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band shaping without exceeding the 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 coating layers total, alternating HfO2/SiO2 starting with HfO2 at air interface)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, each bounded [20, 200] nm, initialized within ±10% variance around the iteration-08 best thickness vector
soft_objectives: maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maintain smooth spectral transition between bands
favor solutions with higher robustness score
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
all thicknesses within [20, 200] nm range for deposition feasibility
alternating material sequence simplifies process control
fused silica substrate is standard optical material
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance bands centered at wavelengths where n*d = λ/4 for each layer
Recalled knowledge: Increasing layer count broadens the high-reflectance stopband and increases peak reflectance
Recalled knowledge: Deviating from strict quarter-wave thicknesses allows stopband position and width tuning
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 (n≈2.0-2.1 in visible/NIR) and SiO2 (n≈1.45-1.5) provide sufficient index contrast for effective dielectric mirrors
Recalled knowledge: Normal incidence simplifies design by eliminating polarization splitting effects
expected_advantages: 24 layers provide sufficient design freedom for dual-band optimization
Alternating sequence is manufacturable with standard deposition tools
Individual thickness optimization allows finer spectral control than periodic stacks
Fused silica substrate transmits well in both target bands
known_risks: Uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal vs. fewer layers with better thickness distribution; would need comparison runs to settle
Uncertain exact refractive index dispersion of hfo2 and sio2 in the 300-1700 nm range from memory; actual values come from material catalog datasets
Uncertain whether alternating sequence starting with HfO2 is superior to starting with SiO2 for this specific band combination; this is a hypothesis
The ±10% initialization variance around prior best may constrain search if the prior solution is in a local optimum; would need to verify improvement over full random seeding
Recalled quarter-wave rule is approximate; actual optimal thicknesses may deviate significantly from λ/4n predictions
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle (0 degrees). The coating stack alternates HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with HfO2 at the air interface and ending with SiO2 (Lemarchand) at the substrate interface, for 24 total coating layers. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses within bounds [20, 200] nm. Initialize thicknesses within ±10% variance around the best thickness vector from iteration-08 (candidate opt_24layer_dual_band_high_R_low_R__172eaad160ed). Apply 25% reduction to mutation step-size compared to prior rounds. Execute deterministic local refinement (Nelder-Mead) on top-5 candidates before resuming stochastic mutation. Use coherent transfer-matrix method. Evaluate performance across two wavelength bands: 300-450 nm (target: maximize reflectance) and 1000-1700 nm (target: maximize transmittance). Score candidates using dual-band equal-weight objective. Material optical constants (n, k) are read from the material catalog datasets for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand); they are not design variables. Total layer count is fixed at 24. Polarization is unpolarized at normal incidence.
routes.revision_reason: Applied feedback directives: 25% reduction to mutation step-size, ±10% initialization variance around iteration-08 best thickness vector, and deterministic local refinement (Nelder-Mead) on top-5 candidates before resuming stochastic mutation

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 24 layers is the optimal count vs. 20 or 28 layers for this specific dual-band requirement
Whether starting the stack with HfO2 (high-index) vs. SiO2 (low-index) at the air interface affects performance for this band combination
The exact refractive index dispersion curves for hfo2 and sio2 in the 300-1700 nm range must come from material catalog, not from memory
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to produce valid candidates after three refinement rounds with relaxed constraints, the problem may require a different material system or non-planar geometry outside the current execution contract.

expected_observations: best_target_score should rise or remain stable compared to iteration-08 value of 0.7999 if the refined search is effective
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if solutions remain physically valid
valid_candidates count should remain high (≥5) indicating the search space is well-bounded
thicknesses_nm values should show reduced variance compared to full random seeding, clustering near the iteration-08 best solution
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 10 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.5 for three consecutive rounds, reduce mutation step-size by another 25% and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
